# Summary of the Labour Party Manifesto 2019

The Labour Party's 2019 manifesto, titled "It's Time for Real Change," presents a comprehensive vision for transforming Britain under the leadership of Jeremy Corbyn. The document addresses what Labour identifies as a decade of Conservative failure across multiple fronts: the economy, climate crisis, public services, and Brexit.

## Core Economic Vision

Labour proposes a fundamental restructuring of the economy through a National Transformation Fund of £400 billion, with £250 billion dedicated specifically to a Green Transformation Fund. The plan includes creating a National Investment Bank and regional development banks to provide £250 billion in enterprise lending over ten years. Central to their economic approach is bringing utilities—rail, mail, water, and energy—into public ownership and delivering free full-fibre broadband nationwide through a nationalised British Broadband service.

## Green Industrial Revolution

The manifesto positions climate action as an urgent priority, committing to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by the 2030s. Key proposals include creating one million green jobs, building 7,000 offshore wind turbines and 2,000 onshore turbines, upgrading 27 million homes for energy efficiency, and banning fracking. Labour pledges to make Britain's industrial sector the greenest globally while supporting workers through the transition.

## Public Services

The NHS would receive average annual funding increases of 4.3%, with commitments to end privatisation, abolish prescription charges, and provide free dental check-ups. Social care reform features prominently, with Labour promising free personal care for older people and a National Care Service. Education proposals include a National Education Service offering free lifelong learning, abolition of tuition fees, restoration of maintenance grants, and 30 hours of free childcare for 2-4 year olds.

## Workers' Rights

Labour proposes establishing a Ministry for Employment Rights, introducing a Real Living Wage of £10 per hour, banning zero-hours contracts, and giving workers full rights from their first day of employment. The manifesto also commits to strengthening trade unions and implementing sectoral collective bargaining.

## Brexit Resolution

Labour promises to resolve Brexit within six months by negotiating a new deal protecting jobs and rights, then putting this deal to a public referendum alongside the option to remain in the EU.
